Chapter Ten: Claiming a Future—Agency, Imagination, and the Ongoing Struggle
You know, the journey doesn’t really stop with one big breakthrough or a single act of escape. For this young man—and honestly, for so many people walking a similar path—the fight for agency keeps going. It's something that has to be worked at every day, as hope and reality tug at each other. There's the world as it stands, and then, there’s the world as it could be.
He keeps writing. He keeps speaking up. He keeps pushing against boundaries that once felt impossible to move. His words find new listeners, spark new conversations, and invite others to question, to dream, and to take action. And now, he’s mentoring younger writers, passing on the lessons he’s learned along the way—the value of being honest, why resilience matters, and how powerful our imagination can really be.
Sure, the world still isn’t perfect. Racism, poverty, injustice—they haven’t disappeared. Sometimes they show up in new ways. Other times, it’s the same old story. But here’s what’s changed: this young man isn’t powerless anymore. He’s discovered that agency isn’t something you’re just handed—it’s something you practice. It’s about moving through life with intention, and refusing to let anyone else draw the lines around what’s possible for you.
He finds his joy in the little wins. Maybe it’s a story published, a letter from a reader who felt seen, or just a simple moment of connection with a stranger. He celebrates progress, even if it's just a small step forward, and he learns to find real meaning in the struggle that never quite ends.
And maybe most important of all, he realizes that imagining a better future—that act alone—is a form of resistance. It’s how you keep hope alive, day after day.
